agent_review.author: agent

findings.summary: The third clone ended in an authoritative whiteout, so the two-win streak is invalid and resets to Clone 1.

resolution.observed: The losing Coppertop bundle was retired. A new exact opening checkpoint contains Bugatti in Coppertop's slot and a new behavior hash; the old bundle cannot be retried.

findings.summary: Coppertop's 7-8 damage required too many Sunflora turns, allowing Grass Whistle and Leech Seed to consume both Coppertop and Birdlaw before Dustox.
findings.observed_fact: Coppertop fell asleep and fainted at full-health Sunflora; Birdlaw was then slept, reached Dustox at 11 HP, and fainted after one Aerial Ace.

resolution.observed: RAM verifies Bugatti at level 17 with Bug/Poison typing, 27 Speed, Bug Bite, Protect, and full HP in the prepared party. Bugatti resists both damaging Sunflora types, outspeeds it, and replaces the weak Tackle line.

findings.summary: Three sleep-prevented actions let Sunflora recover and depleted the reserved Dustox finisher; the old roster was not robust to verified Grass Whistle variance.

resolution.observed: The new profile assigns Bugatti as the Sunflora converter and preserves Birdlaw for Dustox. Qualification restarts under the new hash and must prove the correction three times.

findings.summary: The losing line expanded to 31 actions, 7 switches, and 3 status-prevented actions.

correct_choices: No voluntary Pokémon switched in and back out without acting; the switch-spam defect remained fixed.
Coppertop stayed in while asleep when every replacement was unsafe under the critical entry bound.
Birdlaw committed to its super-effective attacks rather than starting a switch relay.
Every action and the terminal whiteout were verified from emulator state.
agent_review.next_test: Restart Clone 1 from the Bugatti opening checkpoint and verify that Sunflora is removed without exposing Birdlaw to repeated Grass Whistle turns.
